en.title: Non-Friend Recommendation with the Most Mutual Friends
en.description:
For each person, recommend a user who is neither that person nor a direct friend, preferring the most mutual friends and then the smallest ID. A user with 0 mutual friends is still a candidate; return −1 only when there are no non-friends at all. The original OCR input is an edge list, not the matrix of the old curated page; the formal conditions of the original do not require a positive mutual count.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site; missing numeric bounds and recoveries of source typos are all stated explicitly.
en.input: The first line contains n m, followed by m lines of undirected edges. Original range of the complete same problem: 1≤n≤100000, 0≤m≤250000, IDs 0..n−1; there are no self-loops or multi-edges, each person has at most 15 friends, and the graph may be disconnected. The 1-based typo in the body of problem 18 is restored to 0-based according to the original constraints and examples.
en.output: Output n recommended IDs, in order of users 0..n−1.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 3 2 1 0 1; -1 -1 -1; 2 2 0. These answers were verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Enumerate the friends of each person's friends to count two-hop occurrences, excluding the person and their direct friends; if there is no candidate with a positive score, scan for the smallest ID not in the set formed by the person and their friends.
